Hemp was lobbied against by the lumber (for paper) and cotton companies, to have it outlawed in the 30's.

One of the other things holding hemp back are laws. For example, in South Dakota you're only able to grow and harvest hemp if its THC levels are below a certain threshold, and these levels can change based on things like temperature and the amount of water they get, which can often be out of a farmer's control. If THC levels get too high, then you have to destroy your crop. Inspectors from the state must also clear your harvest which slows things down and makes it more expensive.
